article.headline: Free Blender Plugin Brings AI Motion Capture to Any Desk
article.lede: A free plugin now lets Blender users perform AI-driven motion capture on an ordinary consumer PC, no specialized suit or studio required. It runs entirely on local hardware, processing footage through a 10-billion-parameter AI model without sending data to the cloud. The catch is modest: a graphics card with at least 8 GB of VRAM.
article.body:
**Motion capture** — the process of recording a performer's movement and mapping it onto a 3D character — has long belonged to studios with six-figure budgets and rooms full of infrared cameras. This plugin collapses that barrier by substituting computer vision for physical markers, turning a standard 1080p webcam or any pre-recorded video into a usable input signal.

The workflow integrates directly inside Blender, the open-source 3D suite that has become the default tool for independent animators. Users can either feed the plugin a video file or capture live via a connected camera, with the AI inferring skeleton pose frame by frame. The underlying model, at roughly 10 billion parameters, sits in the same weight class as compact but capable language models — substantial enough for plausible pose estimation, small enough to run on consumer GPUs.

The hardware floor is the meaningful constraint. An 8 GB *VRAM* (video RAM, the memory on a graphics card) requirement for real-time capture rules out the cheapest consumer cards but is comfortably within reach of any mid-range GPU sold in the last few years. Offline processing from uploaded video presumably relaxes the real-time bottleneck, though the sources do not specify a lower VRAM tier for that mode.

The significance is less technical than economic. Professional *mocap* pipelines routinely cost tens of thousands of dollars in equipment and studio time. A free, locally-executed alternative — however imperfect relative to optical suits — gives indie game developers, solo animators, and students a tool that simply did not exist at this price point eighteen months ago. Blender's plugin ecosystem has a history of absorbing advances from research labs and turning them into accessible production tools; this appears to be another such moment.

concepts.definition: A technique for recording the movement of people or objects and translating it into digital data, typically to animate 3D characters. Traditional systems use physical markers and infrared cameras; AI-based approaches infer pose from ordinary video instead.

Video RAM — the dedicated memory on a graphics processing unit (GPU). Real-time AI inference loads large model weights into VRAM; insufficient VRAM forces slower system-memory fallbacks or prevents the model from running at all.
A computer-vision task in which an AI model infers the position and orientation of a human body's joints from a 2D image or video frame. It is the core technology enabling markerless motion capture.
